title: Jana Gana Mana at Monaco: Mahindra Racing Ends Five-Year Drought with Historic Formula E Victory
excerpt: Nyck de Vries' masterclass in strategy and energy management delivers India's only global motorsport team their first win in the Gen3 era
body:
The Indian national anthem rang out across the Monaco harbour on Friday evening — not from a diplomatic ceremony or a Bollywood premiere, but from the podium of the Formula E World Championship. Mahindra Racing, India's sole representative in a major global motorsport series, had just won their first race in five years.

Nyck de Vries, the Dutch former Formula One driver who joined Mahindra at the start of the 2025-26 season, delivered a masterclass in energy management and racecraft to claim victory at the 2026 Monaco E-Prix. It was his fifth career Formula E win but his first since Berlin in 2022 — and, more importantly, Mahindra's maiden triumph in the Gen3 era of the championship.

## A Victory Built on Strategy

The Monaco street circuit, with its narrow barriers and minimal overtaking opportunities, has always rewarded precision over raw pace. De Vries understood the assignment. Starting from a strong qualifying position, the Dutchman deployed his PIT BOOST and ATTACK MODE activations with surgical timing, opening a three-second gap that he nursed to the chequered flag.

Behind him, the race descended into chaos. Dan Ticktum tangled with Antonio Felix da Costa in an aggressive late-race battle, earning a 33-second penalty that dropped him from a potential podium to 12th place. Mitch Evans, the Jaguar driver who has been the championship's most consistent performer this season, slotted into second — extending his lead in the Drivers' World Championship by 15 points. Pepe Martí completed the podium in third, becoming the first Spanish driver to stand on a Formula E rostrum.

## Five Years in the Wilderness

For Mahindra Racing, the victory ends what can only be described as a wilderness period. The Pune-headquartered team — the only Indian-registered constructor in any FIA world championship — last won a race in Season 8. The Gen3 era, which introduced faster, more powerful cars, had been particularly unkind. Multiple podium droughts, driver changes, and a painful 840-day gap without a top-three finish had tested the team's resolve.

"This is not just a win for me — it's a win for every single person in the factory in Banbury and in India who never stopped believing," de Vries said after the race. The team's resilience was palpable; engineers who had worked through years of near-misses finally had their moment in motorsport's most glamorous principality.

The victory was also de Vries' 50th Formula E race start — a milestone he marked in the best possible fashion. Since his shock departure from Formula One after a single season with AlphaTauri in 2023, the Dutchman has rebuilt his career methodically, first in the World Endurance Championship with Toyota and now back in the electric series where he won his first world title in 2021.

## What It Means for India

Mahindra Racing occupies a unique space in Indian sport. Unlike cricket teams or individual athletes, it represents India on the global motorsport stage — a domain where the country has historically been a spectator rather than a participant. The sight of the tricolour rising above the Monaco harbour carries a symbolism that extends beyond points and podiums.

For the Indian diaspora, the victory resonates on multiple frequencies. In the UK, where Formula E has a growing television audience, Mahindra's success puts an Indian brand alongside Jaguar, Porsche, and Nissan in the winner's circle. In the United States, where electric vehicles are reshaping the automotive industry, the Mahindra name — already familiar through its agricultural machinery and tech investments — gains a new layer of credibility.

The Mahindra Group's commitment to the championship, now spanning over a decade since Formula E's inaugural season in 2014, has been one of the longest-standing investments in Indian motorsport. Chairman Anand Mahindra has frequently used social media to champion the team's progress, and this victory — India's anthem echoing through the tunnels of Monte Carlo — will be hard to top.

## The Road Ahead

De Vries' triumph lifts Mahindra in the Teams' Championship, though the season remains a tight affair with several rounds remaining. Evans leads the Drivers' standings, but the competitive depth of the Gen3 field means multiple teams remain in mathematical contention.

For Indian motorsport fans — whether watching from Mumbai living rooms or streaming in Mountain View apartments — Monaco 2026 marks a rare moment of arrival. In a world where India's sporting identity is overwhelmingly defined by cricket, a Formula E victory in the principality offers a glimpse of a broader future. And for Mahindra Racing, after five years of building, believing, and waiting, the drought is finally over.
